name: Agriculture, forestry & fishing
characteristic: Primary production of food, fibre and timber from land and water.
positive_test: A grower, forest manager, fishery or land-management agency is the party whose yield, stock or land-use decision the work informs.
negative_test: Not the plant, soil, animal or ecosystem science behind it (Plant Biology, Soil Science, Ecology -> discipline), and not habitat protection for its own sake (-> environment & natural resources).
notes: Thinnest substantive branch (5 mentions). Kept because primary production is a section of every sector standard and a plausible future partner sector for a Quebec institute.

name: Crop & livestock production
characteristic: Growing crops and raising animals on managed land.
positive_test: The decision belongs to a farm or an agricultural extension service: what to plant, when to irrigate, how much land to convert.
negative_test: Not agronomy or plant physiology as knowledge; not remote sensing as a modality.
examples: Crop yield forecasting; Precision agriculture; Livestock monitoring

name: Forestry
characteristic: Managing and harvesting standing forest as a resource.
positive_test: A forest manager or timber operator acts on the result (inventory, growth, harvest, change).
negative_test: Forest monitoring aimed at carbon or habitat rather than yield belongs to environment & natural resources.
examples: Forest inventory estimation; Timber harvest planning; Canopy height mapping
notes: Boundary with biodiversity-and-conservation is genuinely fuzzy; the tiebreak is whether the name mentions yield/stock (forestry) or species/habitat (conservation).

name: Fishing & aquaculture
characteristic: Capture fisheries and farmed aquatic production.
positive_test: A fishery, fish farm or fisheries regulator owns the decision.
negative_test: Marine ecology and ocean modelling as science -> discipline.
examples: Stock assessment; Fishing effort estimation; Aquaculture health monitoring
notes: Zero corpus support. Kept as a declared blind spot, not as a claim: it is an ISIC division and its absence is a finding about this institute.

name: Manufacturing
characteristic: Physical transformation of materials into products inside a plant.
positive_test: A plant, line or process owner acts on the result: throughput, yield, product quality, energy per tonne.
negative_test: Not materials science, chemistry or mechanical engineering as knowledge (-> discipline), and not the design of a molecule or material (-> discipline).
notes: Deliberately excludes drug discovery and materials discovery; see RATIONALE S2.

name: Process industries
characteristic: Continuous or batch transformation of bulk materials (chemicals, metals, pulp, cement).
positive_test: The unit of control is a process (a reactor, a rolling stand, an absorption column), and the owner is a plant operator.
negative_test: Reaction chemistry, catalysis and thermodynamics as science -> discipline.
examples: Steel rolling process control; Chemical plant yield optimization; Industrial carbon capture operation
notes: Carbon capture is filed here, not under energy: the corpus surface is an industrial absorption process, not a power-plant retrofit.

name: Discrete manufacturing
characteristic: Production of countable, assembled or cut items, where the unit of control is a job or a part.
positive_test: A production planner, shop floor or quality function owns the decision.
negative_test: Job-shop scheduling as an OR problem class is machinery -> Method; only a named plant or product line puts it here.
examples: Sawmill production planning; Assembly line quality inspection; Predictive maintenance of machine tools
notes: One corpus name. Retained because process/discrete is the manufacturing sector's own primary division and a one-child parent is not admissible.

name: Energy & utilities
characteristic: Producing and distributing energy, water and waste services over a network to metered customers.
positive_test: A utility, grid operator, system operator or market participant acts on the result.
negative_test: Not energy as physics or battery chemistry (-> discipline); not the energy cost of training a model (-> Desired properties > Frugal AI); not the energy bill of a single building (-> built environment).
notes: Deviation: ISIC keeps D (electricity, gas) and E (water, waste) apart; merged here because E has one corpus name and "utilities" is the register a funder uses. The merge is exactly NAICS 22.

name: Electricity generation & grid operations
characteristic: Generating, transmitting, distributing, storing and trading electric power.
positive_test: The object is a network of generators, feeders, storage and loads that someone must keep balanced.
negative_test: Power electronics and machine design as engineering knowledge -> discipline 2.2.
examples: Renewable generation forecasting; Optimal power flow; Distribution grid demand response
notes: Storage sits here rather than as a sibling: the corpus surfaces are grid- and building-side assets, not a separate utility service.

name: Water & waste services
characteristic: Treating and distributing water, and collecting and treating waste and wastewater.
positive_test: A water utility or municipal service owns the plant or the network.
negative_test: Hydrology and water chemistry as science -> discipline.
examples: Drinking water treatment control; Leak detection in distribution networks; Wastewater quality prediction

name: Built environment
characteristic: Planning, constructing and operating buildings and urban space.
positive_test: An owner, facility manager, designer or planning authority acts on the result.
negative_test: Not structural mechanics or civil engineering as knowledge (-> discipline 2.1); not the grid-side view of building load (-> energy & utilities).
notes: Deviation: ISIC splits construction (F), real estate (L) and planning services (M71); no one of them holds the corpus cluster, and "built environment" is the established cross-sector term.

name: Building operations
characteristic: Running an existing building: comfort, energy, occupancy, maintenance.
positive_test: The decision is made by whoever operates the building, on a time scale of hours to seasons.
negative_test: Grid-level demand response with no named building -> energy & utilities.
examples: Building energy consumption forecasting; HVAC control for thermal comfort; Occupancy-driven building automation

name: Design & construction
characteristic: Designing and erecting a structure, up to handover.
positive_test: An architect, engineer-of-record or contractor acts on the result.
negative_test: Structural analysis methods and materials testing as knowledge -> discipline.
examples: Building information modelling; Construction schedule risk prediction; Automated design code checking
notes: Single corpus name; retained as one of three life-cycle stages.

name: Urban planning & development
characteristic: Deciding how land and urban space are allocated and developed.
positive_test: A municipality, planning authority or developer acts on the result.
negative_test: Urban sociology and social geography as knowledge -> discipline 5.7; traffic operations -> transportation.
examples: Land use classification for zoning; Urban growth scenario modelling; Accessibility mapping for service siting

name: Transportation & logistics
characteristic: Moving people and goods, and running the services and networks that do it.
positive_test: A carrier, transit agency, road authority, shipper or terminal operator acts on the result.
negative_test: Not vehicle or aerospace engineering as knowledge (-> discipline 2.2/2.3); not routing as an OR problem class (VRP, TSP -> Method).
notes: Branch-level residence: `Transportation Networks` names the sector and nothing narrower.

name: Public transit
characteristic: Planning and operating scheduled passenger services.
positive_test: A transit agency owns the timetable, the vehicle block or the crew roster.
negative_test: Crew and vehicle scheduling stated as a pure OR problem with no agency named -> Method.
examples: Bus schedule reliability prediction; Vehicle and crew scheduling; Transit demand forecasting
notes: This is the branch the owner's fleet-routing example points at; `Vehicle and Crew Scheduling Problem` is admitted because crew scheduling names the agency's workforce, not an abstract routing problem.

name: Road traffic & automated vehicles
characteristic: Operating road traffic and road vehicles, including automated driving.
positive_test: A road authority, municipality or vehicle manufacturer acts on the result.
negative_test: Robotics, perception and control as knowledge -> discipline; simulation engines as machinery -> Method.
examples: Traffic signal control; Autonomous driving collision avoidance; Ride-hailing fleet dispatch
notes: The axis's most contestable claim: `Autonomous Driving` (5) names a product capability, not an activity. Admitted because its operational owner is unambiguous; see RATIONALE.

name: Air transport
characteristic: Operating aircraft and air services.
positive_test: An airline, airport or air navigation service provider acts on the result.
negative_test: Aerospace engineering as knowledge -> discipline 2.3.
examples: Aviation emissions estimation; Flight delay prediction; Aircraft system health monitoring

name: Freight & logistics
characteristic: Moving and storing goods: rail, maritime, intermodal terminals, warehousing, distribution.
positive_test: A shipper, carrier, terminal or warehouse operator acts on the result.
negative_test: Network design and routing as OR problem classes -> Method.
examples: Intermodal train load planning; Terminal yard scheduling; Distribution network demand planning
notes: Notable blind spot inside a claimed node: the corpus contains no `Supply Chain` name at all, although AXES.md 7b cites `Supply Chain Optimization` as a canonical example of this axis. The example is invented, not corpus-derived.

name: Information & communication
characteristic: Producing, carrying and servicing information: networks, software and content.
positive_test: A network operator, software organization or content business acts on the result.
negative_test: Not computer science, networking theory or information theory as knowledge (-> discipline 1.2/2.2); not the AI system itself (-> Desired properties).

name: Telecommunications
characteristic: Operating networks that carry signals to subscribers.
positive_test: A carrier or network operator acts on the result: coverage, capacity, handover, power draw, quality of service.
negative_test: Channel estimation, coding and modulation as machinery -> Method; `Computer Networks` and `Communication Systems` as fields -> discipline 2.2.
examples: Radio access network optimization; Cell handover prediction; Satellite link scheduling
notes: Homonym resolved: `Energy Efficiency` (1) is RAN power consumption under a QoS constraint, not Frugal AI. `Parallel Transmission` and `Radio Frequency Interference Mitigation` look like telecom and are not (MRI pTx coils; radio astronomy).

name: Software & IT services
characteristic: Building, shipping, operating and securing software systems as an organized activity.
positive_test: A development team, IT operation or security function acts on the result.
negative_test: Program analysis, fuzzing, mutation testing and repair algorithms are machinery -> Method; code generation and summarization are Task names -> Task; securing the *model* -> Desired properties.
examples: Technical debt management; CI pipeline failure prediction; Vulnerability detection in production code
notes: Largest node on the axis and the one to challenge first. `Software Engineering` (36) is claimed by BOTH axes under rule S-D3. Homonym declared: `Industry 4.0` (2) is software ecosystems here, not manufacturing. Cybersecurity is folded in as depth-3 rather than promoted, to keep this sibling set three industries rather than two industries and a function.

name: Media & entertainment
characteristic: Producing and distributing content: games, film, music, publishing, creative work.
positive_test: A studio, publisher, platform or cultural institution acts on the result.
negative_test: Audio, music and video as signals -> Modality; recommendation as an output type -> Task; misinformation and toxicity as societal problems with no single operational owner are not claimed.
examples: Automated game playtesting; Catalogue recommendation for streaming; Assisted animation authoring
notes: Fused name kept: "media & entertainment" is the sector's own established label, so it is not a compound-name violation. Deviation: ISIC files games under J58.21 publishing and live arts under R90; both are held here.

name: Finance & insurance
characteristic: Intermediating money and risk: banking, payments, investment, insurance.
positive_test: A bank, payment processor, asset manager, insurer or regulator acts on the result.
negative_test: Economics and econometrics as knowledge -> discipline 5.2; portfolio optimization posed purely as a QP is machinery -> Method; `Model Risk Management` in the corpus is AI risk, not bank model risk -> Desired properties.
examples: Payment fraud detection; Portfolio construction under cardinality constraints; Credit risk scoring
notes: Leaf L1: four mentions give no basis for splitting banking from insurance, and inventing the split would fail the >=2-substantive-children rule honestly rather than formally. Insurance is a declared blind spot (zero corpus names).

name: Environment & natural resources
source_code: no ISIC section (spans E39, O84.12, A02, S94)
characteristic: Managing the natural environment as an operational mandate, by what is being managed: ambient quality, living systems, or hazards.
positive_test: An environment ministry, conservation authority, protected-area manager or civil-protection agency runs a programme that consumes the result.
negative_test: Climate science, ecology, conservation biology and earth science as knowledge -> discipline 1.5/1.6; species distribution modelling as a method -> Method/discipline.
notes: Branch-level residence: `Environmental Monitoring` (4) names the mandate and nothing narrower. The one L1 with no ISIC section behind it. Justified in RATIONALE: environmental management has real operational owners, ~13 corpus mentions, and filing it under public administration would hide it from the reading a funder actually wants.

name: Environmental quality & emissions
characteristic: Ambient air, water and land quality, and the emissions that drive them, as a reported and regulated quantity.
positive_test: An agency or operator is mandated to measure, report or reduce the quantity.
negative_test: Atmospheric and hydrological science itself -> discipline 1.5; the energy cost of ML -> Desired properties > Frugal AI.
examples: Air quality monitoring networks; Greenhouse gas emission inventories; Effluent compliance monitoring
notes: AXES.md 2 cites `Greenhouse Gas Emissions Analysis` as the application-domain half of the Green-AI collision; this node is where it lands.

name: Biodiversity & conservation
characteristic: Protecting species and habitat as a managed programme.
positive_test: A conservation authority, protected-area manager or monitoring network acts on the result.
negative_test: `Conservation Biology` and `Ecology` name the science -> discipline; `Species Distribution Modeling` names a method -> Method.
examples: Camera-trap species monitoring; Protected-area spatial prioritization; Bioacoustic survey pipelines
notes: Tight boundary: the corpus has ~15 further biodiversity names (`Conservation Biology` 4, `Biodiversity Modeling`, `Biodiversity Informatics`, `Ecological Modelling`) that are all rejected as science. Stretching to catch them would double this node and is the exact failure mode the brief warns against.

name: Hazards & disaster response
characteristic: Detecting natural hazards and running the response to them.
positive_test: A civil-protection, fire or emergency-management agency acts on the result.
negative_test: Seismology and fire ecology as science -> discipline.
examples: Wildfire detection and spread forecasting; Earthquake early warning; Post-disaster logistics routing

name: Public administration
characteristic: The business of governing: making, evaluating and enforcing public policy and delivering public safety.
positive_test: A ministry, agency, regulator or legislature acts on the result.
negative_test: Political science, economics and law as knowledge -> discipline 5.5/5.6; governing *AI itself* is reflexive -> Desired properties; delivering health, education or transport is filed under those sectors.
examples: Policy option simulation; Programme impact evaluation for a benefits scheme; Trafficking network detection for law enforcement
notes: Leaf L1. `AI Governance` (3), `AI Policy` (2), `AI Regulation`, `Governance of AI`, `Artificial Intelligence Governance`, `AI Safety and Regulation` (2), `Regulatory Science` -- about 10 mentions -- are deliberately NOT claimed: their object is the AI system, which AXES.md 2 makes reflexive and gives to Desired properties. Declared blind spots: defence, taxation, benefits administration, courts, immigration -- all zero.

name: Education
characteristic: Teaching, training and assessing learners in an institution.
positive_test: A school, university, faculty, training programme or licensing body acts on the result.
negative_test: Educational psychology and the learning sciences as knowledge -> discipline 5.3; `Spaced Repetition` as a learning technique -> Method/discipline.
notes: Absent from AXES.md 7b's candidate list; added. ISIC section P, ~26 corpus mentions -- the fourth-largest branch on the axis. Its omission from the candidate list is a schema defect, not a corpus finding.

name: General & higher education
characteristic: Teaching in schools and universities.
positive_test: The learner is a student in a degree or school programme and an institution owns the curriculum.
negative_test: Learning as a cognitive phenomenon -> discipline 5.1.
examples: Intelligent tutoring for mathematics; Student dropout prediction; Automated programming-assignment feedback

name: Professional & continuing education
characteristic: Training and assessing practitioners already inside a profession.
positive_test: A residency programme, professional college or employer owns the training and the assessment.
negative_test: The clinical or technical content being taught -> discipline; a simulator as machinery -> Method.
examples: Surgical skill assessment from video; Simulation-based clinical training; Competency examination scoring
notes: Cost accepted deliberately, stated the way AXES.md 7 states the neuroscience split: the ~16-mention medical-education cluster is filed under Education, not Healthcare, so no single node totals "all health-sector work". A NodeCut can report either, but not their sum.

name: Healthcare & social care
characteristic: Delivering, organizing and paying for health and social services.
positive_test: A provider, hospital, payer, ministry of health, public-health agency or social-service agency acts on the result.
negative_test: Clinical and biomedical specialties name bodies of knowledge, not operations: `Medical Imaging`, `Oncology`, `Psychiatry`, `Radiation Therapy`, `Epidemiology` -> discipline 3.x only.
notes: Heavy branch-level residence, exactly as AXES.md 8b predicts: 45 of this branch's 154 mentions (29%) sit at depth 1, on umbrella surfaces (`Healthcare` 16 plus the AI-in-healthcare family) that name the sector and nothing narrower. Any depth-2 share must be quoted against a denominator that names this bucket.

name: Clinical services
characteristic: Delivering care to patients, through any channel.
positive_test: A clinician, service line or care pathway is the thing being planned, triaged, supported or extended.
negative_test: The disease, the modality and the specialty -> discipline; a diagnostic model as machinery -> Method/Task.
examples: Emergency department triage support; Clinical decision support at the point of care; Remote monitoring in chronic disease
notes: Digital health and telemedicine are folded in as delivery channels rather than made a sibling; a channel is not an actor, and the branch divides by actor.

name: Patient & caregiver support
characteristic: Serving the patient and the family rather than the clinician.
positive_test: The result changes what a patient or an informal caregiver knows, decides or experiences.
negative_test: Health communication as a social science -> discipline 5.8; patient outcome prediction for clinicians -> clinical services.
examples: Shared decision-making aids; Patient-reported experience analysis; Caregiver support tools

name: Health system administration
characteristic: Running the system rather than treating the patient: information, access, policy, resources.
positive_test: A hospital administrator, health authority, payer or ministry acts on the result.
negative_test: `Health Economics` and `Pharmacoeconomics` study markets as phenomena -> discipline 5.2; `Epidemiology` -> discipline.
examples: Hospital resource and bed planning; Health record data quality auditing; Equity of access analysis
notes: The informatics surfaces are claimed by both axes: their object is the care system's information machinery, which is a human-run operating system (rule S-D3). `Bioinformatics`, whose object is biological data, is discipline-only -- the contrast is the rule working.

name: Public & population health
characteristic: Acting on the health of a population rather than a patient.
positive_test: A public-health agency runs surveillance, prevention or a programme.
negative_test: `Epidemiology` (20) and `Epidemic Modeling` name the science and the method -> discipline/Method.
examples: Syndromic surveillance; Outbreak early warning; Population screening programme targeting
notes: `Public Health` (12) is the cleanest genuinely-both name on the axis: a school-of-public-health discipline and a government function. Claimed by both, per AXES.md 7b's own `Operations Management` precedent.

name: Social care & community services
characteristic: Non-medical care and protection services for people who need support.
positive_test: A social-service agency, care home or community programme acts on the result.
negative_test: Gerontology, social work and developmental psychology as knowledge -> discipline 5.1/5.4; a clinical geriatrics specialty -> discipline 3.2.
examples: Child protection case risk screening; Assistive technology for ageing in place; Home care scheduling

name: Retail & consumer services
characteristic: Selling goods and services to consumers, and the pricing, marketing and demand planning that go with it.
positive_test: A retailer, brand, hospitality operator or advertiser acts on the result.
negative_test: Consumer psychology and marketing science as knowledge -> discipline 5.1/5.2; `Recommender Systems` fails "exists without AI" and is a Task.
examples: Retail demand forecasting; Booking and revenue management; Ad targeting and bidding
notes: Leaf L1, five mentions. The largest available stretch on the whole axis is here and is refused: routing `Recommender Systems` (16) plus its variants to retail would roughly double the node on a name AXES.md 7 already assigns to Task. Deviation: advertising is ISIC M73, held here because its customer is the brand.

name: Uninformative
characteristic: Administrative row, not a sector. On-axis surfaces that name an economic activity but no sector.
positive_test: The name is about operations, commerce or industry in general, and a reader learns nothing about which sector from it.
negative_test: A name that simply says nothing about this axis is absent from the axis, not uninformative (AXES.md 8b).
examples: Industry; Operations management; Business analytics
notes: Excluded from this axis's shares. Note that `Operations Management` -- AXES.md 7b's own headline example of a name that "maps in both axes" -- lands here on the sector side: it is on-axis but names no sector.

name: Software product engineering
characteristic: Producing and maintaining the software artefact itself as a team practice: requirements, design, code, review, test, debt, maintenance.
positive_test: A development team acts on the result: how the code is specified, written, reviewed, tested, documented or kept maintainable.
negative_test: Program analysis, fuzzing, mutation testing, test generation and repair as algorithms are machinery -> Method; `Code Generation` and `Summarization` are Task names (S5); running the system in production -> IT operations.
notes: Largest depth-3 node on the axis; carries the `Software Engineering` (36) family, which rule S-D3 claims on BOTH axes. Indicative support ~55 mentions.

name: IT operations & service management
characteristic: Running software and IT services in production for an organization: release, deployment, incident, configuration, capacity.
positive_test: An IT operation, SRE or platform function owns the result, and the object is a system already in service.
negative_test: Designing or repairing the code itself -> software product engineering; selling the capacity the system runs on -> cloud & data-centre services.
notes: Indicative support ~4 mentions (`DevOps`, `MLOps`, `Continuous Integration`, `Software Reliability Engineering`).

name: Cloud & data-centre services
characteristic: Selling compute, storage and hosting capacity as a service.
positive_test: A hosting or cloud provider acts on the result: placement, utilisation, scheduling of a shared platform, SLA, facility operation.
negative_test: The energy cost of training a model is reflexive -> Desired properties > Frugal AI; distributed and parallel training as machinery -> Method; a data centre seen as an electrical load -> energy & utilities.
notes: SPECULATIVE: zero corpus support. `Edge Computing` and `Mobile Edge Computing` are rejected at level 2 as technologies (S2). Kept per AXES.md 9 -- a node with no support is kept and flagged, never deleted.

name: Cybersecurity operations
characteristic: Defending deployed systems, code and data against adversaries, as an operational function.
positive_test: A security function acts on the result: vulnerability, intrusion, malware, incident response, forensics.
negative_test: Attacking or defending the MODEL is reflexive -> Desired properties / Method (rule S6; `Machine Learning Security` 3 is declined here); cryptography and security theory as knowledge -> discipline 1.2/2.2.
notes: Depth-3 by RATIONALE 5.3: every sector has a security function, so it is not a sibling of two industries. Indicative support ~10 mentions.

name: Care operations & capacity
characteristic: Planning and running the capacity that delivers care: beds, theatres, staff rosters, appointments, patient flow.
positive_test: The object is a schedule, a roster, a queue or a capacity decision owned by a hospital or service manager.
negative_test: The clinical decision inside the encounter -> clinical services; scheduling stated as an OR problem class with no provider named -> Method (S4).
notes: SPECULATIVE: no clean corpus support. `Scheduling` and `Personnel Scheduling` are refused at level 2 as too generic / OR problem classes even though one quote is physician scheduling. WHO building blocks: service delivery + workforce.

name: Health information systems & records
characteristic: Running the information machinery of care: records, coding, interoperability, data quality, registries.
positive_test: The object is the care system's information flow -- what is recorded, by whom, in what standard, and whether it can be reused.
negative_test: `Bioinformatics`, whose object is biological data, is discipline-only; a prediction model built ON records is Method/Task unless the record system itself is what is managed.
notes: The both-axes block of rule S-D3 (`Health Informatics` 8, `Healthcare Informatics` 4, `Medical Informatics`, `Biomedical Informatics`, `Health Data Science`). Indicative support ~18 mentions. WHO building block: information.

name: Health financing & coverage
characteristic: Paying for care and deciding what is covered: reimbursement, claims, cost, utilisation, benefit design.
positive_test: A payer, insurer or ministry acts on the result, and the object is money moving through the health system.
negative_test: `Health Economics` and `Pharmacoeconomics` study markets as phenomena -> discipline 5.2; general insurance underwriting -> finance & insurance.
notes: SPECULATIVE: zero corpus support. DEVIATION: ISIC files health insurance under K65.12 and compulsory health insurance under O84.30, outside section Q; held here because the payer is part of the health system in the register a funder reads. WHO building block: financing.

name: Health policy, planning & governance
characteristic: Setting priorities, configuring services across a system and regulating them, including access and equity planning and health technology assessment.
positive_test: A ministry, health authority or regulator acts on the result at the level of a programme or a system, not a patient.
negative_test: Political science, law and economics as knowledge -> discipline 5.2/5.5/5.6; governing AI itself is reflexive -> Desired properties (S6).
notes: `Access & equity` was drafted as a fifth sibling and folded in here by the property test: access can be true of operations, financing and policy alike. Indicative support ~6 mentions. WHO building block: governance.

name: Disease surveillance & outbreak response
characteristic: Watching the health of a population and running the response to what is detected: notification, early warning, investigation, tracing, emergency response.
positive_test: A public-health agency operates a surveillance system or an outbreak response, and the result changes what it detects or how it responds.
negative_test: `Epidemiology` (20) and `Epidemic Modeling` name the science and the method -> discipline / Method; pathogen biology -> discipline 3.1.
notes: Indicative support ~5 mentions (`Public Health Surveillance` 3, `Outbreak Detection`, `Infectious Disease Monitoring`).

name: Prevention & health promotion programmes
characteristic: Running programmes that act before disease occurs: immunisation, screening, risk-factor and behaviour programmes, targeting and uptake.
positive_test: The agency runs a programme aimed at a population that is not yet ill, and the result changes its design, targeting or reach.
negative_test: Vaccinology and immunology -> discipline 3.1; screening as a diagnostic model -> Method/Task; individual clinical prevention inside a consultation -> clinical services.
notes: THIN: indicative support 1 mention (`Injury Prevention`); `Vaccinology` and `Vaccine Immunology` are discipline. Flagged near-speculative.

name: Environmental & occupational health protection
characteristic: Protecting a population from exposures in the environment and the workplace, as a health mandate.
positive_test: The mandate named is a health outcome in a population exposed to something.
negative_test: Ambient quality as a regulated environmental quantity -> environment & natural resources > environmental quality & emissions; toxicology and atmospheric science -> discipline 1.4/1.5.
notes: THIN: indicative support 1 mention (`Environmental Health`). Boundary tiebreak with the environment branch is the mandate named: a health outcome here, a regulated ambient quantity there.

name: Primary & community care
characteristic: First-contact and continuing care in the community, owned by a general practice or community clinic.
positive_test: The care-delivery organization named is a general practice, community clinic or community programme.
negative_test: A specialty as a body of knowledge -> discipline; social and non-medical community support -> social care & community services.
notes: Indicative support ~2 mentions (`Community-based Primary Health Care`, `Prenatal Care`).

name: Hospital & acute care
characteristic: Care delivered inside a hospital episode: emergency, inpatient, critical and peri-operative services.
positive_test: The setting is a hospital or an emergency service and the result changes how that episode is run.
negative_test: Hospital capacity, beds and rosters -> health system administration (the administrator, not the clinician); `Pediatric Surgery` (16) and other specialties -> discipline 3.2.
notes: Indicative support ~5 mentions (`Emergency Medical Services`, `Emergency Care`, `Trauma Care` 2, `Pediatric Trauma Care`).

name: Specialist & ambulatory care
characteristic: Scheduled specialist consultation, diagnostic and day-treatment services outside an inpatient episode.
positive_test: The object is the RUNNING of a specialist or ambulatory service: referral, access, clinic throughput, day-treatment pathway.
negative_test: A specialty name (`Oncology`, `Radiology`, `Medical Imaging`, `Pediatric Surgery`) is a body of knowledge and is discipline-only; this node is never claimed because a specialty is mentioned.
notes: SPECULATIVE: zero corpus support. The single most dangerous node on the axis: it is one word away from re-importing the ~200 mentions of clinical specialties that level 2 refused. Its negative test is deliberately stricter than its positive one.

name: Rehabilitation & continuing care
characteristic: Clinical care after the acute episode: rehabilitation, chronic follow-up, home-based clinical care and clinician-owned remote monitoring.
positive_test: A clinician or clinical service remains responsible for a patient outside an acute episode.
negative_test: Non-medical residential and home support -> social care & community services; what the patient or family does for themselves -> patient & caregiver support; `Geriatrics` as a specialty -> discipline.
notes: SPECULATIVE / weak: at most 1 indicative mention (`Healthcare and Chronic Diseases`). Kept because a care system without a continuing-care setting is not a care system.

name: Entry-to-practice training
characteristic: Training a novice into a licensed practitioner: residency, clerkship, apprenticeship, supervised practice.
positive_test: A training programme owns the learner's progression towards the right to practise.
negative_test: The clinical or technical content being taught -> discipline; a simulator or a video model as machinery -> Method / Modality.
notes: The whole professional-education cluster lands here: indicative support ~12 mentions (`Medical Education` 7, `Surgical Education`, `Simulation in Surgical Training`, `Non-technical Skills Training`, `Medical Training and Education`).

name: Continuing professional development
characteristic: Keeping qualified practitioners current after qualification, run by an employer or a professional association.
positive_test: The learner already practises, and an employer or association owns the training.
negative_test: Initial qualification -> entry-to-practice training; assessment for a licence -> certification & licensure.
notes: SPECULATIVE: zero corpus support.

name: Certification, licensure & competency assessment
characteristic: Examining, scoring, certifying and licensing practitioners against a standard.
positive_test: A college, board or examining body acts on the result: scoring, standard-setting, competency measurement.
negative_test: Regulating a profession in general rather than its training -> public administration; `Examination and Assessment Techniques` in the corpus is LLM benchmarking -> mark_ignore (AXES.md 8b).
notes: SPECULATIVE: zero corpus support, although the level-2 row's own examples name it. The corpus's professional-education cluster is entirely training-side.

name: Patient information & decision support
characteristic: Helping a patient understand options and reach a decision with a clinician.
positive_test: The result changes what a patient or family knows or decides at a decision point.
negative_test: Clinical decision support aimed at the clinician -> clinical services; health communication as a social science -> discipline 5.8.
notes: Indicative support ~8 mentions (`Shared Decision Making` 5+1, `Patient Decision Aids Evaluation`, `Patient-Centered Care`, `Doctor-Patient Communication`).

name: Self-management & home support
characteristic: Helping a patient or family carry out care day to day: adherence, self-monitoring they own, assistive support at home.
positive_test: The patient or the informal caregiver is the one who acts on the result, in their own home and on their own initiative.
negative_test: Clinician-owned remote monitoring -> clinical services > rehabilitation & continuing care; non-medical home support arranged by an agency -> social care & community services.
notes: SPECULATIVE: no clean corpus support (`Patient Support Systems` 1 reads as clinician-facing). Weakest node in the weakest sibling set on the axis; see DEPTH3_RATIONALE.

name: Patient experience & voice
characteristic: Collecting and acting on what patients and families report about their care.
positive_test: The patient's own report (experience, outcome, complaint, preference) is the object.
negative_test: A provider-owned quality dashboard is administration -> health system administration. Tiebreak: whose instrument it is, the patient's report or the manager's measure.
notes: Indicative support 2 mentions (`Patient Experience` -- quote confirms PREMs -- and `Patient Care Experience`).

name: Power generation
characteristic: Operating generating assets and forecasting their output.
positive_test: A generator owner or operator acts on the result: availability, output, dispatchability of a plant or fleet.
negative_test: Generation technology as engineering knowledge (turbines, PV physics, battery chemistry) -> discipline 2.2/1.3.
notes: Indicative support 1 mention (`Renewable Energy Forecasting`).

name: Transmission & system operation
characteristic: Keeping the bulk power system balanced and secure: flow, commitment, reserves, congestion, stability.
positive_test: A transmission or system operator is responsible for the state of the network as a whole.
negative_test: Power-flow formulations posed purely as optimization problem classes -> Method (S4); power electronics -> discipline 2.2.
notes: Indicative support ~2 mentions (`Optimal Power Flow`, `Smart Grids`); `Power Systems` 3 names the branch and sits at level 2.

name: Distribution & grid-edge operations
characteristic: Running the distribution network and the flexible resources connected to it: DERs, EV charging, demand response, metering, outages.
positive_test: The decision sits at or below the substation: a feeder, a meter, a flexible load or a customer-side asset.
negative_test: The building's own energy bill with no network view -> built environment > building operations; the energy cost of ML -> Desired properties > Frugal AI.
notes: Default home for STORAGE, which is a technology cross-cutting the whole chain rather than a sibling (property test). Indicative support ~6 mentions.

name: Electricity markets & trading
characteristic: Buying, selling and pricing electric power.
positive_test: A market participant, market operator or regulator acts on the result: bids, prices, settlements, market design in operation.
negative_test: Auction theory and mechanism design as machinery -> Method; energy economics as a field -> discipline 5.2.
notes: Indicative support 1 mention (`Energy Market Modeling`).

name: Mobile & wireless networks
characteristic: Operating radio access networks that serve mobile subscribers: coverage, capacity, handover, scheduling, power.
positive_test: A mobile operator owns the cells, the spectrum or the radio resource being managed.
negative_test: Channel estimation, coding and modulation as machinery -> Method; `Wireless Communications` as a field of study -> discipline 2.2; `Radio Frequency Interference Mitigation` is a declared homonym (radio astronomy).
notes: Carries almost all of this node's corpus: indicative support ~7 mentions (`Cellular Network Optimization` 2, `5G Communications`, `Wireless Networks`, `Self-Organizing Networks`, ...). `Energy Efficiency` (1) is declared here as RAN power, not Frugal AI.

name: Fixed & core network operations
characteristic: Operating wireline access and the transport core that carries aggregated traffic.
positive_test: A carrier operates fixed access or backbone capacity, routing or traffic engineering for subscribers.
negative_test: `Computer Networks` and `Communication Systems` as fields -> discipline 2.2; datacentre load balancing is IT -> software & IT services (declared homonym `Network Optimization`).
notes: SPECULATIVE: zero corpus support; every telecom name in the corpus is wireless or satellite.

name: Satellite & non-terrestrial networks
characteristic: Operating satellite and other non-terrestrial links as a carrier service.
positive_test: The operator runs the space or aerial segment and its links as a communication service.
negative_test: Earth observation from satellites is a sensing activity, not a carrier service -> environment / agriculture, with remote sensing as Modality; orbital mechanics -> discipline.
notes: Indicative support 2 mentions (`Satellite Communication`, `Satellite Communication Systems`).

name: Games & interactive entertainment
characteristic: Making and running interactive entertainment products: development, playtesting, content generation, live operation.
positive_test: A studio or publisher acts on the result: what ships, what is tested, what players are served.
negative_test: `Game Theory` (20) supplies machinery -> Method; `Game Playing` as an RL benchmark names no sector -> Method/Task; game engines as simulators -> Method.
notes: Indicative support ~5 mentions (`Game Development`, `Game Design and Analysis`, `Automated Game Testing`, `Game Testing`, `Serious Games`). Declared homonym: `Game Theory` / `Game Playing` are NOT this node.

name: Screen & recorded media production
characteristic: Producing film, television, video, animation, recorded music and sound.
positive_test: A studio, production house or label owns the production process the result changes.
negative_test: Audio, music and video as signals -> Modality; generation and separation as output types -> Task; the node needs a production activity, not a signal.
notes: THIN: indicative support 1 mention (`3D Animation`). The music and video names in the corpus (`Music Generation`, `Music Source Separation`, `Automatic Music Transcription`) are Modality/Task names, not production activities.

name: Publishing & news media
characteristic: Producing books, periodicals and journalism, and running the editorial process.
positive_test: A publisher or newsroom acts on the result: what is commissioned, edited, fact-checked or printed.
negative_test: `Misinformation Detection` and `Fact-checking` are refused at level 2 by S3 -- platforms, newsrooms and regulators are all plausible owners and none is named; text summarization -> Task.
notes: SPECULATIVE: zero corpus support, and the nearest corpus cluster is deliberately unclaimed.

name: Broadcasting & content platforms
characteristic: Programming, scheduling and serving a catalogue to an audience.
positive_test: The operator of the channel, catalogue or platform acts on the result: what is carried and what an audience is served.
negative_test: `Recommender Systems` (16) fails 'exists without AI' and is a Task (S1+S5); only a task name qualified by a sectoral object lands here.
notes: Indicative support ~4 mentions (`Cultural Content Recommendation` 2, `Movie Recommendation`, `Music Recommendation Systems`) -- exactly the S5 qualified-task case, and it is the reason the node exists.

name: Arts, culture & heritage
characteristic: Running performing arts, museums, archives and collections as institutions, and supporting creative practice inside them.
positive_test: A cultural institution or a working artist acts on the result.
negative_test: Creativity as a cognitive phenomenon -> discipline 5.1; generation as an output type -> Task; `Art Therapy` is a care activity -> healthcare.
notes: THIN: indicative support ~3 mentions (`Creativity Support Tools` 2, `Creative AI`). Exists because deviation D4 holds R90 inside this branch.

name: Traffic management & road operations
characteristic: Running the road network itself: signals, flow, incidents, tolling, enforcement.
positive_test: A road authority or municipality owns the network asset the result acts on.
negative_test: Traffic flow physics and transport modelling as knowledge -> discipline; routing posed as an OR problem class -> Method (S4).
notes: Indicative support ~3 mentions (`Traffic Signal Control` 2, `Traffic Scene Generation`). The clearest sector-only cluster in this branch.

name: Automated & assisted driving
characteristic: Operating the vehicle itself under automation or driver assistance.
positive_test: A vehicle manufacturer or automated-fleet operator acts on the result.
negative_test: Perception, planning and control as knowledge -> discipline 2.2/2.3; driving simulators as machinery -> Method; `Autonomous Systems` (2) is a technology, refused at level 2 (S2).
notes: Inherits RATIONALE 5.4: `Autonomous Driving` (5) names a product capability, not an activity, and is the axis's weakest claim. Isolating it in its own depth-3 node makes the reversal cheap -- delete this row and the traffic-operations nodes are untouched. Indicative support ~6 mentions.

name: Road passenger mobility services
characteristic: Running on-demand and shared road passenger services: ride-hailing dispatch, fleet rebalancing, shared vehicles.
positive_test: A mobility operator owns a fleet and the assignment of vehicles to customers.
negative_test: Scheduled fixed-route services -> public transit; vehicle routing posed as an OR problem class -> Method (S4).
notes: Indicative support 1 mention (`Autonomous Mobility on Demand`; the quote names a central operator dispatching vehicles to customer requests, which is S3 passing cleanly). Declared boundary: road FREIGHT haulage (H49.41) is filed with freight & logistics by function, although the parent row's code range nominally includes H49.4.

name: School education
characteristic: Teaching and assessing in primary and secondary schools.
positive_test: A school, school board or ministry of education owns the curriculum and the learner is a school pupil.
negative_test: Learning as a cognitive phenomenon -> discipline 5.1; educational sciences as a field -> discipline 5.3 (which also claims the sector names, per S-D3).
notes: SPECULATIVE: no corpus name states the segment. Every education name in the corpus (`Educational Technology`, `Educational Data Mining`, `Intelligent Tutoring Systems`, `Programming Education`) is segment-blind and sits at the parent by branch-level residence (AXES.md 8b).

name: Higher education
characteristic: Teaching, supervising and assessing in degree-granting tertiary institutions.
positive_test: A university, college or faculty owns the programme and the learner is a degree student.
negative_test: Training practitioners already inside a profession -> professional & continuing education; research itself is ISIC M and excluded axis-wide (deviation D6).
notes: SPECULATIVE: same as `school-education`. `Computer Science Education` and `Programming Education` name a SUBJECT, not a segment, and are not evidence for this node.
